_notes:
Microchip MCP9600, MCP9601 and MCP96L01 thermocouple EMF to temperature converters (with cold-junction compensation) at 0x67 (the Adafruit boards' default, ADDR pin unconnected), 0x66 or 0x63. Of their eight addresses (0x60-0x67) the others aren't claimed: 0x60 (VCNL4040), 0x61 (SCD30), 0x62 (SCD40) and 0x64-0x65 (STCC4) are other records' addresses, where this record's probeByRead would change how the scanner probes those parts too
probeByRead: after an address-only (zero-length) transfer - the usual scan probe - the chip stops answering until power is cycled (bench, Axiom018, 2026-11-08, an MCP9601: five ID reads, one zero-length write that it ACKed, then every access NACKed), so the scanner probes these addresses with a 1-byte read
Detection: device ID/revision (0x20), 2 bytes: ID 0x40 (MCP9600) or 0x41 (MCP9601, MCP96L01), any revision
Init: sensor configuration (0x05) = 0x00 - type K, filter off; device configuration (0x06) = 0x00 - normal mode, 18-bit ADC, 0.0625 C cold-junction resolution (both the power-up values, written in case they were changed)
Poll (500 ms; a conversion takes about 320 ms at 18 bits): hot junction (0x00, the thermocouple temperature, compensated), cold junction (0x02, the chip's own temperature), each big-endian signed 16-bit at 0.0625 C; status (0x04). openCircuit (bit 4) and shortCircuit (bit 5) are the MCP9601's and MCP96L01's thermocouple checks (the MCP9600's bit 4 is input out of range, bit 5 unused). With no thermocouple the hot junction value means nothing
Source: registers from the Microchip MCP960X/L0X/RL0X datasheet (DS20005426); the status bits as Adafruit_MCP9601 names them
